title: Remove legacy X-Redwood headers, upgrade client transports, and harmonize dep matrix
creator: Asha Patel
description: This ticket coordinates coordinated client library dependency upgrades (Python, JS, Go) and the safe removal of legacy X-Redwood-* request/response headers that were kept for backwards compatibility. The goal is to simplify transport surfaces, reduce middleware overhead, and remove after-market compatibility branching inside SDKs that costs CPU and adds complexity to caching/batching logic.
background: Over the last 18 months we introduced several legacy headers (X-Redwood-Trace, X-Redwood-Version, X-Redwood-Compat) to aid migration from monolithic runtime endpoints to the new routing stack. Those headers are now stale and create branching in SDK transports. Additionally, each language client carries different versions of HTTP libraries and ad-hoc shims (requests/httpx fetch polyfills, node-fetch vs native fetch vs undici, net/http wrappers in Go) that complicate testing and cause perf variance.
goals: 1) Remove internal handling of legacy X-Redwood-* headers from SDK transports and stop sending them by default. 2) Upgrade and pin canonical transport libraries: Python -> httpx 1.1.x, JS -> undici 5.x (node 18+ native fetch fallback), Go -> net/http minimal wrapper + retry middleware. 3) Reduce cold-path allocations in transports and shave ~5-12% CPU on high-throughput workloads. 4) Provide clear migration guides and a compatibility shim release for one major version cycle.
scope:
- Modify client transports in python-sdk, js-sdk, go-sdk
- Add integration tests to interoperability matrix and perf harness
- Publish migration guide and deprecation notice
- Rollout canary builds to 5 internal services, run for 2 weeks, then general release
non_goals:
- Not touching public API surface beyond transport header removal (no semantic change to request/response fields).
- We will not backport deep kernel/runtime changes in this ticket.
tasks:
1) Audit all places where X-Redwood-* headers are set or read (search across repo + downstream sample apps).
2) Implement opt-out flag in each SDK (send_legacy_headers: boolean) defaulting to false for the new major release and true for the compatibility minor.
3) Upgrade transport dependencies and consolidate retry/backoff code paths.
4) Add unit and integration tests that assert headers are not sent and that new transports respect timeout/retry semantics.
5) Add performance microbenchmarks (tokens/sec, CPU/sample) to CI perf gate.
6) Draft migration guide and deprecation blog post with explicit curl/SDK examples.
7) Coordinate with Console/Runtime teams for rollout windows and API-side acceptance (strip headers server-side after canary).
8) Cut client releases: python 3.0.0 (major bump), js 4.0.0, go v2.0.0.
9) Post-release monitoring and rollback automation (feature flag to re-enable legacy headers server-side for emergency rollbacks).
acceptance_criteria:
- All three SDKs default to not sending legacy headers in the released major version.
- CI perf gate shows no regression and ideally 5-12% CPU improvement on benchmark workload compared to baseline.
- Integration tests pass with runtime in canary region when server-side header stripping is enabled.
- Migration guide published and linked from SDK README.
- No customer-facing incidents within 14 days of GA; if incidents occur, rollback plan executes within <30 minutes.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests: header presence/absence, opt-out flag behavior.
- Integration: end-to-end against canary runtime that simulates legacy header semantics.
- Performance: run benchmark harness (bench/tokents_per_suite) in CI fleet under three concurrency profiles; compare CPU and latency P95 to baseline.
- Compatibility: smoke tests with top 10 OSS customers and internal sample apps.
- Chaos: simulate partial network failures and retries to verify backoff behavior.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal canary (5 internal services) with client pre-release and runtime configured to accept both modes. 2) Gradual external canary by opt-in customers (Documentation + early access). 3) After 2 weeks and green metrics, publish GA and release major client versions. 4) Server-side header strip enabled globally 7 days after GA (to give customers time to upgrade).
monitoring_and_migration:
- Dashboards: token throughput, client error rate, model latency, server header-parse rate.
- Alert: spike in 4xx/5xx from SDKs or sudden drop in throughput tagged "sdk-transport".
- Migration: customers can enable legacy header passthrough via account toggle for up to 30 days. We will email active customers and add in-console banner.
- Migration assist: engineering on-call dedicated for first 72 hours post-GA.
risks:
- Some older customer deployments rely on X-Redwood-Compat for routing and will experience muted failures if they don't upgrade. Mitigation: account toggle + server passthrough.
- Transport upgrades may surface subtle timeout/retry differences. Mitigation: extensive integration and perf testing.
- Unexpected perf regressions on Node 16 environments; mitigation: keep node 16 fallback path for one release and call out min supported node 18 in docs.
notes:
- This ticket intentionally consolidates transport changes to minimize repetitive major bumps across tiny tickets.
- We will coordinate client major bumps with SDK release cadence to avoid dependency chaos.
- Consider a follow-up ticket to remove opt-out flags after 1 major version window.
timeline:
2025-02-10: ticket created
2025-02-18: audit complete
2025-02-24: transport PRs opened
2025-03-05: integration perf gates green (this update)
2025-03-10: internal canary start
2025-03-22: GA release target
rollback_plan: If we detect customer-impacting regressions: 1) Re-enable server-side passthrough toggle immediately. 2) Publish patched client with opt-in legacy headers flag and notify customers. 3) Open follow-up hotfix and schedule retro to remediate.
communication:
- Pre-announcement email to active SDK consumers 10 days before GA.
- In-console banner linked to migration guide.
- Changelog entries in each SDK with migration steps and example diffs.
postmortem_criteria: Any outage or >1% sustained error rate increase attributable to transport changes will require a full postmortem with RCA and action items.
implementation_details:
- Python: migrate to httpx 1.1.x async and sync client flavors; remove legacy header middleware; add send_legacy_headers flag on Client init.
- JS: adopt undici pool when available, fallback to global fetch for Deno/browser; strip legacy-header paths in fetch wrapper; publish major.
- Go: remove ad-hoc header plumbing in net/http wrapper; provide small opt-in compat transport implementation in examples rather than shipping in main module.
